extracted.intended_audience: general NPR readers interested in news, digital media ethics, and popular culture
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and norms for creating or assessing online video content (vlogs) that depict suicide, graphic scenes, or culturally sensitive material, with emphasis on ethical conduct, platform policy, and harm-minimization. Useful for journalists, creators, moderators, and critics judging such videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform policy on violent/gory content
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube says that Paul's video violates its policies against presenting violent or gory content in a way that is sensational or disrespectful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present graphic/violent or gory imagery in sensationalizing or disrespectful ways; platforms may remove or take enforcement action on content that treats such material as entertainment or spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for the dignity of suicide victims
rubrics_metrics.description: "That body was a person someone loved. You do not walk into a suicide forest with a camera and claim mental health awareness." (Anna Akana)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exploiting or objectifying victims. Filming, close-ups, or treating a corpse as 'content' violates ethical norms; consider the deceased and their loved ones and refrain from intrusive recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make suicide or mental illness the subject of jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Suicide is not a joke. Depression and mental illnesses are not a joke."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor that trivializes, mocks, or jokes about suicide/mental illness is inappropriate and harmful; creators should avoid comedic framing of self-harm or mental-health crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blurring faces is insufficient if other identifying or graphic details are shown
rubrics_metrics.description: Paul blurred out the face of the person who had died, but he showed other parts of the body as he and his friends stood near it and talked — which drew criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any graphic details or identifying elements remain visible, simple face-blurring does not mitigate harm. Best practice is to avoid showing the scene at all; remove or heavily edit footage that reveals body parts or personal items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent does not excuse harmful impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Paul said "I intended to raise awareness for suicide and suicide prevention...I was misguided by shock and awe," but critics said intent doesn't justify the harm caused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators' claimed intentions (e.g., raising awareness) do not absolve them of responsibility for negative consequences; evaluate content by its impact, not only stated purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove and demonetize content that causes harm
rubrics_metrics.description: The site confirms that Logan Paul took the video down. Paul said that he had "demonetized" the video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content is clearly harmful or violates norms/policies, creators and platforms should remove it and consider demonetization or other limits to prevent incentivizing similar content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using shock, 'shock and awe', or pursuit of views as justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Paul's earlier messaging ('tomorrow's vlog will be the craziest and most real video I've ever uploaded' and calling the site 'content gold') and critics' comments highlight concerns about seeking views via sensationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize clicks or sensationalism over ethical considerations; sensational framing for views is an antipathetic practice and increases risk of harm to subjects and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect local cultures and avoid mocking when abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: The apologies come as Paul has also been criticized for mocking Japanese culture during his visit to the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators working in other countries should be culturally sensitive, avoid stereotypes or mockery, and not treat a culture as a backdrop for crude jokes or exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide suicide-prevention resources when dealing with suicide-related content
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube works with the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline — and displays suicide prevention resources at the top of the results for YouTube searches related to suicide. The article lists the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content touches on suicide or self-harm, include clear, accessible information about prevention resources and helplines to direct viewers who may be at risk toward help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not harass or taunt potential victims; contact authorities instead
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge reports: the group's guide phones the police while they approach the body, shouting 'Yo, are you alive, are you fooling with us?' They film the apparent suicide victim up close...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach suspected medical or traumatic incidents by contacting emergency services; avoid confrontational or performative behavior and do not film in ways that further distress the victim or interfere with aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize meaningfully and acknowledge mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Paul released a video apology saying, 'I should have never posted the video; I should have put the cameras down, stopped recording what we were going through. There's a lot of things I should have done differently... I am sorry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A responsible apology should admit specific failures, state corrective action (e.g., removing content), and commit to different behavior going forward rather than offering only vague regret or excuses.
